FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Charlotte FC face Chicago Fire at Bank of America Stadium in MLS's Round One, game two of the series. Charlotte FC lead the series 1-0 after winning the first game 2-1 away at Chicago Fire. A Charlotte FC win takes them through, while a Chicago Fire win levels the series and forces another game.

Current Form - Charlotte FC

Charlotte FC finished fifth in the Eastern Conference with 54 points from 34 matches, recording 15 wins, nine draws and 10 losses, with a 66-51 season scoreline. Their recent five-match record is three wins, one draw and one loss, while their last play-off game ended in a 2-1 win away at Chicago Fire. Charlotte FC have gone four matches without defeat. They scored 3.0 goals per match across that recent window, compared with 1.9 across the season, and conceded 1.4 per match against a season figure of 1.5.

Current Form - Chicago Fire

Chicago Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference with 55 points from 34 matches, posting 16 wins, seven draws and 11 losses alongside a 64-54 season scoreline. Their recent five-match record is two wins, one draw and two losses, and their last play-off game was a 1-2 home loss to Charlotte FC. Across the recent window, Chicago Fire scored 2.6 goals per match against 1.9 for the season, while their conceding figure rose to 2.4 from 1.6.

Head-to-Head Record

The last five meetings have produced an average of 3.4 goals. Charlotte FC won one and lost four of those meetings. Chicago Fire have won their last two meetings away at Charlotte FC, every one of them since May 2025. Earlier this season, Charlotte FC beat Chicago Fire 2-1 at Chicago Fire's home venue.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Pep Biel, a midfielder for Charlotte FC, has 14 goals and 10 assists. Forward Liel Abada has 11 goals and five assists in 28 games, including six goals across his last four matches, scored in three of them. Allan Saint-Maximin, also a forward, has two goals and four assists in 15 games. Nathan Byrne is a doubt with an injury, while Archie Goodwin is unavailable with a foot injury.

Robert Lewandowski has 10 goals and four assists in 20 games for Chicago Fire, with four goals across his last three matches, scored in three of them. Forward Philip Zinckernagel has seven goals and nine assists in 34 games, while midfielder Maren Haile-Selassie is Chicago Fire's top scorer with 13 goals and eight assists. Noah Allen is a doubt with a muscle injury.

Match Notes

Allan Saint-Maximin received one red card in Charlotte FC's last 10 matches, with that dismissal coming three matches ago. Mbekezile Mbokazi has collected four yellow cards in Chicago Fire's last 10 matches, across nine appearances. Brandt Bronico is now with Charlotte FC after coming from Chicago Fire, where he made 66 appearances and scored two goals across four seasons, six seasons ago.
